📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

Understanding Data Science Key Concept

To comprehend this definition let us take an example.

Data Science Process Key Concept

Data science is a systematic and iterative process.

Goal Identification Key Concept

This is the first stage in any data science project.

Data Collection Key Concept

The next stage in your data science project is to gather the relevant data.

Data Preparation Key Concept

This is the step where we prepare the retrieved data for exploratory analysis and modelling.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

1.2 Understanding Data Science

  • To comprehend this definition let us take an example.
  • Imagine a critical 11 Data Science Fundamentals care unit in a multi-specialty hospital where patients are normally put on mechanical ventilation.
  • Mechanical ventilation while lifesaving, also incurs risk of Ventilator-Induced Lung Injury (VILI).
  • Optimal mechanical ventilation and weaning strategy is required.

1.3 Data Science Process

  • Data science is a systematic and iterative process.
  • When new insights or issues arise, data scientists frequently iterate back to previous steps.
  • Goal Identification This is the first stage in any data science project.
  • It aims to understand the business problem and determine the objectives of the investigation.

1.3.1 Goal Identification

  • This is the first stage in any data science project.
  • It aims to understand the business problem and determine the objectives of the investigation.
  • This demands a grasp of the project's ‘what’ and ‘why’.
  • Upon completion of this phase, you can generate a project charter.

1.3.2 Data Collection

  • The next stage in your data science project is to gather the relevant data.
  • Data scientists typically encounter two types of situations: - Adequate data exists inside the organisation.
  • - No data is available within the organisation, or the existing data is insufficient.
  • In the first scenario, data is often accessible in the organization's formal repositories, including databases, data marts, data warehouses, and data lakes.

1.3.3 Data Preparation

  • This is the step where we prepare the retrieved data for exploratory analysis and modelling.
  • It involves cleaning the data by removing errors in your data, combining data retrieved from different sources, and converting the data into a certain shape for all further analysis.
  • Data cleaning ensures that errors, inconsistencies, and outliers are removed.
  • Data integration combines datasets from different sources, while data transformation prepares the data for modelling by reshaping variables or creating new features.

1.3.4 Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

  • It serves as a foundation for understanding the underlying structure of the data, identifying important variables, and guiding subsequent modeling efforts.
  • EDA typically involves techniques such as distribution analysis, correlation assessment, and outlier detection, often using tools like histograms, box plots, scatter plots, and heatmaps.
  • By providing insights into the quality and nature of the data, EDA helps data scientists make informed decisions about data preprocessing, feature selection, and modeling strategies.
  • Its role is not only diagnostic but also strategic, as it enables a deeper Once you have all the data you need and have put it in the right format, the next step is to understand it and pick the right modelling methods.

1.3.5 Model Development

  • Predictions, object classification, or system comprehension, as sought in the first stage of data science, are the main aim of this stage.
  • While the exploratory data analysis step focuses on identifying general trends in the data, this step is more focused on the goal of the overall data science project.
  • In this step, machine learning or deep learning models are normally built to make predictions or classifications based on the data.
  • This step heavily relies on statistics, data mining, and machine learning.

1.3.6 Model Deployment and Presentation

  • Once the analysis is completed and insights have been derived, the findings are communicated to stakeholders through reports, dashboards, or presentations.
  • This stage plays a vital role in decision-making and often leads to the deployment of data science models into real-world environments.
  • Deployment involves integrating these models with existing operational systems, such as enterprise software, web applications, or databases.
  • However, this integration is not always straightforward and may present a range of technical and organizational challenges.
